description: Grep at D: the version-control baseline (PREREGISTRATION.md section 11), an agent that answers each item's question by reading its arm's tree as of the end of the item's date and the log beside it, the files at D and git-log.txt, without diffs or earlier versions, with read-only shell commands that run in a sandbox with no route out. systems/harness.py writes its requests, one file for each arm and date, and its answer rows; grep-at-d/run_dates.py builds each date's tree with asofbench materialize, runs that date's requests in grep at D's environment (grep-at-d/compose.yaml) and deletes the tree; the agent (grep-at-d/agent.py) answers in grep at D's own image, built FROM the reader image (grep-at-d/Dockerfile), through the reader's runner, and its commands run in the sandbox (grep-at-d/sandbox); systems/README.md describes them.
inputs: the question text, and in the sandbox its arm's tree as of the end of the item's date: the proposal files as they stood, rebuilt from that arm's episodes by asofbench materialize and named <repo>/<series>-<number>, and git-log.txt beside them, the log of the commits up to that date; nothing else from the repositories, so no header that the arm withholds, no index such as PEP 0 and nothing recorded after the date
entries: every item in every arm that its arms field lists (section 12), each three times (runs 1, 2 and 3); in a pilot run, the items of a list such as data/v0.1/pilot.json (harness.py requests --items)

requests.key: a random UUID4 for each item, arm and run, which says nothing of the item and is never the same twice
requests.layout: one requests file for each arm and date, input/<file>/requests.jsonl, <file> the arm's stream's name and the date (harness.file_name, such as h-minus-2021-09-03), each alone in its directory, with an empty output/<file>/ for its run; dates.json maps each file to its arm and as_of and holds nothing of the items; plan.json records each file's number of requests and SHA-256 and dates.json's SHA-256, and dates.json is written last, after every requests file has its name
requests.order: ascending key order within each file: the keys are random UUID4s, so each file is a random permutation of its items' order, and the requests of one item (its runs) are not next to one another; the reader answers a file in its order and stops after five api_error responses in a row, which must mean a cause that every request shares; keys.jsonl keeps the items' order
requests.kept_on_the_host: keys.jsonl, which maps each key to the item's id, arm, run and answer_type, plan.json and dates.json, and run_dates.py's trees.json, beside the run directory's input/ and output/: a date's run is given that date's input/<file>/, which holds its requests.jsonl alone, read-only, and its output/<file>/; the reader refuses a requests file that is not alone in its directory
requests.never_sent: the item's id, family, stratum, answer_type, proposal, corpus, as_of and every other field, and every other file of data/v0.1; the date is never a field of a request, it chooses the tree that the sandbox holds

prompts.system: You answer one question about a repository of proposal files by reading it with read-only shell commands. The directory /repo holds the proposals' files as they stood at the end of the question's date, each named <repo>/<series>-<number> (the repository, peps, EIPs or ERCs; the series in lower case, pep, eip or erc; and the number, in four digits for a PEP), and git-log.txt, the log of the commits up to that date, newest first, with each commit's time, the files it touched and its message. Use the run tool to look. When you know the answer, reply with a JSON object whose "answer" field holds it in the form the question asks for.

tool.name: run
tool.description: Run a read-only shell command in /repo and return its output. Commands run under bash with a 20 second limit; output beyond 20,000 characters is cut.

prompts.cap_turn: You have used all 40 commands. Reply now with your final answer as the JSON object.

tool_result.text: each command's result goes back as one tool result: its stdout as it came, then, when it has any, a line stderr: and its stderr, then a last line, exit code: N, or for a command that ran past the limit the timed-out line; each part ends with a line break before the next, and an output cut at 20,000 characters ends with its final line [cut: N characters omitted]
tool_result.timed_out_line: the command ran past the 20 second limit and was killed
tool_result.not_run: Not run: the run tool takes one field, "command", a shell command of at most 65,536 bytes.
tool_result.not_run_when: a call of another tool than run, or whose input is not one field, command, a string of at most 65,536 bytes in UTF-8 with no NUL character: it is not run, and its result is this text, marked is_error
tool_result.past_the_cap: a call of the cap's turn past the 40th is not run, and its result is the cap's turn, marked is_error

prompts.model_facing: the system prompt, the user message's text around the question, the tool's name, description and input schema, the labels and lines of the tool results, the not-run result and the cap's user turn are the only text that the model receives besides the question and the commands' output, and hold no benchmark-derived value: no item id, gold value, family name or stratum; the commands' output is the tree's and the log's own text

answering.call: grep-at-d/agent.py answer_with_commands: one messages.create call for each turn, without streaming, with the keyword arguments of asofbench_systems.answer.answering_settings with grep at D's system prompt, and the run tool with tool_choice auto (agent.settings), the same on every turn
answering.sensitivity_check_model: claude-sonnet-5-5, on the pilot items, scored in its own run
answering.tools: the run tool (prompts.tool), which the agent runs in the sandbox, and no other
answering.tool_choice: auto on every turn: the model chooses on each turn whether to call the tool; the registered settings use adaptive thinking, and the tool choice is left at auto with them
answering.not_sent: no temperature, top_p or top_k, so the temperature is the default; no prefill (each turn's messages end with a user turn); no other tool, no server tool, no strict mode and no beta header
answering.scorer_settings: effort medium, adaptive thinking, default temperature

prompt_caching.placement: each request marks its last block, and no other, with this marker: the last block of its last user turn, which is the question on the first turn and then the last tool result or the cap's turn; each turn reads the prefix that the one before it wrote. A block's marker is the multi-turn pattern for anthropic 0.78.0, whose messages.create takes markers on blocks and has no top-level cache_control
prompt_caching.ttl: 5 minutes, the default: each turn follows the one before it within seconds
prompt_caching.effect: a marker that moves is no edit of the history, so thinking blocks stay valid; caching changes no output and no setting, and tokens_in counts the tokens written to and read from the cache with the rest of the input

answering.anthropic_client: asofbench_systems.llm.make_async_client: anthropic.AsyncAnthropic with base_url https://api.anthropic.com given in code (ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL is never read), the key read from the Docker secret /run/secrets/anthropic_api_key only, the SDK's own httpx client honouring HTTPS_PROXY, max_retries 8, timeout 600 s
answering.sdk: anthropic 0.78.0, which sends anthropic-version 2023-06-01: the lowest release whose messages.create takes output_config's effort, the json_schema output format and adaptive thinking (0.77.1 has the format only), as reader/requirements.in records
answering.usage_log: asofbench_systems.usage.instrument wraps client.messages.create and records every turn's call in usage.jsonl under the request's key, the invocation and attempt 1, each line with the model the call asked for and the model id the response named, which can be a dated snapshot of it

transcript.first_turn: the question, Question: {question}, as a user turn of one text block
transcript.append_only: each reply goes back as the API sent it, block for block (thinking and redacted thinking blocks unmodified, text and tool calls), followed by one user turn with a tool result for each of its tool calls, in their order; nothing earlier is ever edited or removed
transcript.commands: a turn's commands run one after another in the sandbox, in their order

limits.cap: after the 40th result the user turn ends with the cap's turn, a text block after the tool results; a call of that turn past the 40th is not run; a tool call after the cap's turn ends the answer with a null answer and the error command_cap, the request's own outcome and never an api_error; a call that is not run counts toward the cap, so that every answer ends

reply.answer: the answer field of the JSON object that the text blocks of the reply that calls no tool hold, as it came (the harness shapes it); thinking blocks before it are passed over
reply.tokens_in: every turn's input_tokens, cache_creation_input_tokens and cache_read_input_tokens, summed (a call that raised counts 0)
reply.wall_s: the answer's wall time in seconds, every turn and command included, with the SDK's retries and the waits for the sandbox
reply.tool_calls: the number of commands run in the sandbox, at most 40; a call that was not run is not counted
reply.thinking_blocks: the thinking blocks of every turn's response, summed: adaptive thinking lets the model answer without thinking, so this records what it did

not_answered.refusal: a response with stop_reason refusal on any turn, whatever it holds
not_answered.max_tokens: a response with stop_reason max_tokens on any turn, whatever it holds
not_answered.unparseable: a reply that calls no tool and whose text is not one JSON object with an answer field
not_answered.api_error: an API error, after the SDK's retries, that is the request's own, such as a 400, 404, 413 or 422, on any turn
not_answered.command_cap: a tool call after the cap's turn

reply.null_answer: a request that was not answered has a response with a null answer and its error code, and its row has a null answer, which scores zero (section 12)

shaping: the harness shapes each answer by the item's answer_type and does nothing else to it: for status, a string is kept, an integer becomes its decimal string, and anything else is kept as it came; for set, a list is kept, a string that parses as a JSON list is replaced by that list, and anything else is kept as it came; for count, an integer is kept, a string of ASCII digits with an optional leading minus sign is replaced by its integer, and anything else is kept as it came. A boolean is no integer. The scorer normalises the rest
rows: harness.py rows writes one row per request, in keys.jsonl's order, with exactly the nine fields of section 12, gathering the responses of every date's output/<file>/ after checking dates.json and each date's requests file against plan.json and each response against its date's keys; a key with no response, which a date that has not run or stopped leaves, gets a null answer and null costs, and rows exits 1; so does a run with a date whose last invocation stopped with exit status 3, whether or not every key has a response: rows writes its rows and says to discard the run and run it again in a fresh run directory

run.runner: the reader's runner, reader/answer_requests.py, which grep at D's image holds from the reader image, with grep at D's answering function, images, network check and self-test (grep_at_d, agent.main), and its requests without a context: a requests file whose lines hold one is another entrant's, and grep_at_d refuses it before anything is answered, with exit status 2; its concurrency, its resume by key, its usage log, its lock, run.json and its stops hold as for the single-call entrants
run.order: the requests file's order, read one line at a time, with 8 calls under way at once
run.infrastructure: an infrastructure error stops the run with exit status 2 and writes no response for its request, so that a resumed run answers it: after the SDK's own retries, the API unreachable, rate-limited, overloaded or failing, or refusing the key (anthropic APIConnectionError, RateLimitError, InternalServerError, AuthenticationError or PermissionDeniedError, the classes that anthropic 0.78.0's client raises for these: InternalServerError for every 5xx, 503, 504 and 529 included, since that client has no branch of its own for 529; the shared table also names OverloadedError, which that client never raises), or the standard library's ConnectionError; the requests under way finish and keep their responses, and no other starts; and a sandbox that cannot be reached, does not answer within 300 s or answers anything but a command's result (SandboxUnavailable, a ConnectionError), which stops the run in the same way: a failure of the environment never gives a request a null answer
run.consecutive_api_errors: 5 api_error responses in a row, in the order they are written, stop the run with exit status 3: each is its request's own error and stays, but so many in a row point at a cause that every request shares, such as a setting that the API rejects, which would give one to every request left; the requests under way finish and keep their responses, and no other starts. A resume answers only the requests that have no response, so a run that stopped this way for a cause of the run is discarded and run again in a new run directory once the cause is fixed, never resumed under changed settings; a resumed run counts on from the api_error responses at the end of the responses file
run.resume: answer_requests --resume answers every request that has no response, after checking that the requests file, the responses file and the model are those that the run began with
run.lock: every invocation holds the output directory's lock, run.lock, created with O_EXCL and touched every 30 s, and removes it at its end; a second invocation on the directory stops at once with exit status 2
run.exit_status: 0 when every request has a response with an answer; 1 when every request has a response and some of them have an error code; 2 when it is refused before it starts, the network check fails or an infrastructure error stops it; 3 when 5 api_error responses in a row stop it; 4 when it crashes, which run.json records with the exception's class
run.dates: grep-at-d/run_dates.py, on the host, runs one environment for each arm and date in dates.json's order: it builds the date's tree with asofbench materialize --arm --data from the arm's registered stream into a fresh directory outside the repository, named tree- and random letters, which say nothing of the arm or the date, under a --trees-dir whose path names no arm, date or user either, since the sandbox's mount table shows the tree's whole path on the host, with every directory 0755 and every file 0644 so that uid 10001 reads it; it hashes the stream again once the tree is built, and deletes the tree and runs nothing when the stream is no longer the registered one; it records the tree in the run directory's trees.json (run.trees); it runs the agent with that date's input/<file>/, output/<file>/ and tree, saves the proxy's log beside the responses, takes the environment down (whose failure stops it) and deletes the tree whatever the run did; a date that is done is skipped, one that stopped with exit status 2 or 4 or was killed is resumed, and one that stopped with exit status 3 stops it, since its run is discarded and never resumed. It checks first that grep at D's image is built on the reader image whose ID the run records (its layers begin with the reader's), and dates.json, each requests file and the build's MANIFEST.json against plan.json; it holds the run directory's lock (run.lock) to its end, and a SIGTERM takes the date under way down, deletes its tree and releases the lock before it stops, with exit status 2, for a later invocation to resume
run.trees: run_dates.py's record of every tree it built, trees.json, beside plan.json and dates.json in the run directory, on the host and given to no container: for each date's file, its arm and as_of, and each tree built for it in the order they were built (a resumed date has one for each attempt), with built_at and the name and SHA-256 of the stream that it was built from, which is the one that the build's manifest registers for the arm (asofbench materialize checks the stream before it reads it, and run_dates.py hashes it again once the tree is built), so that where each date's tree came from can be checked from the run's outputs alone, against the manifest whose SHA-256 plan.json records
run.api_errors_across_dates: the stop after 5 api_error responses in a row spans the dates: each date's run is given --api-errors-before N, the api_error responses in a row that the dates before it ended with, in the order they were answered (dates.json's), counted on from the previous date's count when every one of a date's responses is an api_error and from the api_error responses that it ends with otherwise, and on a resume from the dates already done; the runner counts on from N, so that the fifth in a row stops the run with exit status 3 wherever it falls, and run.json's stop then records N as api_errors_before; run_dates.py stops with exit status 3 and the advice to discard the run and run it again in a fresh run directory

sandbox.image: asofbench/sandbox, built from grep-at-d/sandbox/Dockerfile with that directory as the context; its build ends with the command server's self-test, run with no network
sandbox.packages: bash, coreutils, grep, findutils and sed from the base image, Debian's essential packages, and gawk and python3, for the command server, with their dependencies from http://snapshot.debian.org/archive/debian/20261027T000000Z (trixie and trixie-updates) and http://snapshot.debian.org/archive/debian-security/20261027T000000Z (trixie-security), the archive as it stood when the base image was built, and from no other source. The versions installed are the snapshot's: the base image too was built from the archive as it stood at 20261027T000000Z (its history's debuerreotype timestamp, @1793059200), so the snapshot pin fixes every one of them and a rebuild installs the same; the build's dpkg-query lists them, and installed.sandbox.package_versions records them
sandbox.repo: the date's tree, a read-only bind mount at /repo of the fresh directory that asofbench materialize wrote, which holds the proposal files and git-log.txt and nothing else
sandbox.tmp: a tmpfs of 16 MiB at /tmp, the commands' HOME and TMPDIR, emptied before each command
sandbox.hardening: no capability (cap_drop ALL), no-new-privileges, a private IPC namespace with no /dev/shm (ipc none), an init process that reaps what a command leaves (init: true), no secret, no environment from the host and no published port
sandbox.network: sandbox_net alone, an internal network with no address of the host on it, which only the agent's container shares: no route out, no proxy
sandbox.api: POST /run with a JSON body {"command": str}, answered with {"exit_code", "stdout", "stderr", "truncated", "timed_out"}; every other request is refused, with a status line and a JSON body {"error": ...}, and runs nothing, http.server's own refusals included (grep-at-d/sandbox/command_server.py)
sandbox.commands: each runs as bash -c in /repo, in a session and process group of its own, with stdin from /dev/null and an environment of PATH, LANG and LC_ALL (C.UTF-8), HOME and TMPDIR alone; it ends when bash exits or at 20 s, and then its whole process group is killed, background jobs included; stdout and stderr are each kept up to 20,000 characters, read as UTF-8 with each byte that is not UTF-8 replaced by U+FFFD, and an output that is longer is cut there and ends with a final line [cut: N characters omitted]
sandbox.tools: the agent's commands may use what the sandbox image holds: bash, coreutils, grep, findutils, sed and gawk, and python3, which the command server needs and the commands may run too, with no route out from either
sandbox.one_at_a_time: commands run one at a time, in the order their requests arrive (a ticket for each, served in turn), so that the requests of a date, whose agents share the sandbox, never see one another's processes or scratch files; a command waits for those that came before it, and its answer's wall_s includes the wait
sandbox.stated_limits: a process that a command moves into a session of its own (setsid) leaves the process group that is killed, and lives until the date's environment is taken down; the commands run as the server's user, so one could stop the server, which stops the run with exit status 2

routes_out.through: the egress proxy (env/egress, asofbench/egress) on the internal network, which opens a CONNECT tunnel to that host and port only and refuses everything else
routes_out.for: the answering model, claude-haiku-5-5, or claude-sonnet-5-5 in the sensitivity check, on every turn of the agent's answers

proxy.idle_timeout: EGRESS_IDLE_TIMEOUT in grep-at-d/compose.yaml: the proxy closes a tunnel that neither side has used for 660 s, a minute longer than the client's 600 s request timeout, since a non-streaming request receives nothing until its response begins; a request therefore ends at the client's timeout, never cut short by the proxy
proxy.limits: the proxy's stated limits: it relays TLS uninspected, so it checks the host and port of the CONNECT request and never the server name (SNI) that the TLS handshake sends inside a tunnel to api.anthropic.com:443, which is therefore not checked against the CONNECT host; and it has no cap on concurrent connections
proxy.log: one JSON line per request (ts, client, method, target, allowed, reason) and nothing of what passes through a tunnel; run_dates.py saves it beside each date's responses, as egress.log (egress-<n>.log for a later attempt)

services_inside.name: sandbox
services_inside.what: the command server (grep-at-d/sandbox), which runs the agent's read-only shell commands
services_inside.holds: the date's tree and git-log.txt, read-only, its own software and a scratch directory emptied before each command; nothing else of the host
services_inside.network: sandbox_net alone, which only the agent's container shares; it reaches neither the proxy nor anything beyond the agent's container

network_policy.container: the agent's container, in grep at D's image (the reader image with the agent and its self-test added), is on inner, with the egress proxy, and on sandbox_net, with the sandbox, and sees the reader's runner, the shared package, the network check, the agent and its self-test, the date's requests (input/<file>/, read-only at /input), its output directory (/output) and the API key as a Docker secret; the sandbox's container sees the date's tree, read-only at /repo, and nothing else of the host
network_policy.unreachable: data/v0.1, every file of this repository other than the reader's runner, the agent and its self-test, the shared package, the network check and the command server, the harness's keys.jsonl, plan.json and dates.json, run_dates.py's trees.json, the streams, every other date's tree, the corpus clones, and the corpora's live sources (github.com/python/peps, github.com/ethereum/EIPs, github.com/ethereum/ERCs, peps.python.org, eips.ethereum.org and ercs.ethereum.org), their mirrors or a clone of them
network_policy.provider_side_tools: none: every turn carries the one client-side tool, run, which the agent runs in the sandbox, and no server tool (web search, web fetch, code execution, file search or any other)
network_policy.checked_by: env/netcheck.py, run by grep_at_d before anything is answered, with the flags that every system gives it (asofbench_systems.run.NETCHECK_ARGS), the sandbox (sandbox:7000) as its one service, which must resolve and accept a connection, and the mounts /input, /output and /run/secrets; it aborts the run on any failure, and its report is netcheck.json in the date's output directory; the sandbox's own isolation is checked by hand inside its container (systems/README.md)

installed.lock: reader/requirements.txt, compiled from reader/requirements.in with hashes by uv 0.7.2: the reader image installs it hash-checked, from wheels only, and checks the installed packages against it at its build; grep at D's image, built FROM the reader image, installs no package

images.asofbench/grep-at-d: built from grep-at-d/Dockerfile with systems/ as the context, FROM asofbench/reader by its local tag: the reader image with grep at D's agent and its self-test (grep-at-d/agent.py and grep-at-d/selftest.py, at /app/grep_at_d) and its command, grep_at_d, added, and nothing else; its build ends with grep_at_d --self-test, run with no network
images.asofbench/reader: built from reader/Dockerfile with systems/ as the context, on the base image above, with the packages above: the reader's runner and its self-test, the shared package and the network check, the image the single-call entrants answer in; its build ends with answer_requests --self-test, run with no network
images.asofbench/egress: built from env/egress, on the base image above
images.asofbench/sandbox: built from grep-at-d/sandbox/Dockerfile with that directory as the context, on its own base image and with its own packages (sandbox below); its build ends with the command server's self-test, run with no network

sandbox.packages: bash, coreutils, grep, findutils and sed from the base image, and gawk and python3 and their dependencies from the snapshot, at the versions that package_versions records (sandbox.packages)

installed.per_run: each date's run records in its run.json the IDs of the four images it ran with, grep at D's, the reader's that it is built from, the proxy's and the sandbox's, which its launcher gives in ASOFBENCH_IMAGE_IDS; run_dates.py checks first that grep at D's image is built on that reader image
